title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-03-24
content:
Perf & Benchmarking Sync - 2026-03-24
Attendees: Michael Chen (owner), Asha Patel, Ravi Kumar, Sofia Martinez, Liam O'Connor, plus notes from SRE rotation
Duration: 45m
Location: #perf-sync + Zoom

Agenda:
- Quick status + recent test runs
- Investigate latency/throughput regression reported on 2026-03-22
- Repro steps and scope (models/hardware/batch settings)
- Mitigation plan and rollout guardrails
- Action items + owners

Summary of findings:
- Regression observed: p95 latency increase and throughput drop for redwood-1-small quantized (int8) on H100 nodes after runtime upgrade to 2.8.0.
  - Baseline (runtime 2.7.3) on A100-40GB: p50=38ms, p95=220ms, sustained throughput=420 req/s (batching enabled, max_batch=8, seq=512).
  - Observed (runtime 2.8.0) on H100-80GB: p50=42ms (+11%), p95=260ms (+18%), sustained throughput=330 req/s (-21%).
- Regression is most pronounced at seq_len >= 768 and batch sizes 4-8. Small-seq (<=128) workloads show <5% variance.
- Regressions reproducible in perf cluster (perf-aug-3) but not consistently in dev cluster. Suspect kernel selection/path triggered by runtime change.

What we tested during meeting:
- A/B runs between 2.7.3 and 2.8.0 on same H100 instance type (same CUDA/cuBLAS versions). Result: 2.8.0 consistently slower for large seq.
- Quantization toggle: int8 vs fp16. Int8 shows higher regression magnitude. fp16 shows small non-deterministic variance.
- Model variants: redwood-1-small (fp32->int8 quant) and redwood-1-base. Regression larger on small (attention kernel fusion differences).
- Batch window tuning: increasing batching window from 8ms -> 25ms recovers some throughput but spikes p95 under bursty arrival.

Preliminary root cause hypotheses:
1) Kernel selection change in runtime 2.8.0 picks an H100-optimized matmul kernel that performs worse for small-batched large-seq workloads due to memory access pattern.
2) KV cache memory layout change combined with int8 codepath leads to extra copies when sequence length crosses 512 boundary.
3) CUDA/cuBLAS minor version mismatch between perf cluster nodes causing suboptimal kernel fallback.

Repro steps (short):
1) Checkout serving-runtime at commit used in canary: refs/pull/489 (see linked PR).
2) Start perf job on perf-aug-3 H100 (image: runtime-2.8.0-cuda12).
3) Run loadgen with redwood-1-small-int8, seq_len 1024, concurrency 64, max_batch 8, target qps 400 for 10m.
4) Collect p50/p95 and GPU metrics (sm utilization, mem bw, nvlink).
5) Repeat with runtime 2.7.3 image on identical node.

Short-term mitigations agreed:
- Rollback option: keep a 2.7.3 canary pool for quantized workloads - SRE to re-pin canary nodes (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-03-25).
- Disable int8 auto-quant path on runtime 2.8.0 for models where seq_len > 512 until root cause determined (owner: Asha Patel, due: 2026-03-26).
- Add a perf test that exercises seq_len 768-1536 with batches 4-8 to the CI nightly matrix (owner: Ravi Kumar, due: 2026-03-27).
- Add telemetry flags to trace kernel selection and extra-copy counts for int8 KV cache (owner: Sofia Martinez, due: 2026-03-26).

Longer-term work:
- Perf bisect: run binary search across runtime commits between 2.7.3 and 2.8.0 to pinpoint offending change (owner: Michael Chen + Ravi, start: 2026-03-25).
- Evaluate alternative matmul kernels / tune heuristics for H100 small-batch large-seq (owner: eng-serving-runtime kernel team, logged to JIRA-PERF-1223).
- Improve cluster job reproducibility by locking CUDA/cuBLAS minor versions across perf nodes (owner: SRE, ticket created).

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should we classify this as P1 (impacting customer SLAs)? Current impact: increased tail for specific workloads; few customer incidents but potential SLA risk if we roll 2.8.0 at scale. We leaned toward P2 with immediate mitigations.
- Is there a single flag we can expose to customers to opt-out of int8 path? Short-term: set per-customer model profile to force fp16.

Action items (owner - due):
- Liam O'Connor - Re-pin canary nodes to runtime 2.7.3 and run smoke tests (2026-03-25).
- Asha Patel - Implement runtime-level toggle to disable int8 auto-quant for seq_len > 512 (PR + tests) (2026-03-26).
- Ravi Kumar - Add nightly perf matrix test (seq 768-1536, batch 4-8) and integrate results dashboard (2026-03-27).
- Sofia Martinez - Instrument kernel selection tracing and extra-copy telemetry; upload sample traces to Confluence (2026-03-26).
- Michael Chen + Ravi Kumar - Start bisect across runtime commits (2026-03-25 start).

Notes / misc:
- Linked PR is under review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/489 (changes: kernel selection heuristics, matmul patch).
- JIRA: PERF-1223 created for tracking (linked).
- We observed a transient NVLINK bandwidth saturation on one run; need to confirm whether it's correlated or noise.

Next sync:
- Weekly perf sync: 2026-03-31 10:00 PT. Will provide preliminary bisect results and telemetry dashboards.

Minutes prepared by: Michael Chen
